method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18, the 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 rulings on negatives, and the writing-l4-rules skill; focus: the provisions a claimant meets, here a whistleblower who may suffer a reprisal (what may be disclosed, to whom and how; what the entity must tell; the journalist route; protections; reprisal, damages, vicarious liability, Anti-Discrimination Act complaints, appeals, relocation, injunctions; confidentiality of identity). The s 20(1)(b)(iii) six months is a regulative rule (PARTY ... DO ... WITHIN ... HENCE FULFILLED LEST PARTY ... MAY) and the seat questions read plain dates; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered: ...`, asserted); every judgment of an entity, a manager, the industrial relations commission or a court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2010 (Qld), the version in force from 2024-08-30, current on 2026-11-06, deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2010-038.txt (a plain-text conversion of the HTML view, not the authorised PDF). No regulation deposited; none sets a number used. The Acts Interpretation Act 1954 is not deposited, so periods are reckoned without moving a last day past a weekend or public holiday (NOTES.md fork F15, finding 9).

checks.command: l4 run pidq-dates.l4 ; l4 run pidq-discloser.l4 ; l4 run pidq-cases-discloser.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached or residual DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the regulative rule is asserted through CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED.

scope: In: ss 3, 5-7, 10, 11, 12-17, 19, 20 (ss 21-25 by their effect: they remove conditions), 26, 30, 32, 34 (in an answer), 36-50 (ss 51-56 named), 65, 66, 67(1), 69 (in an answer); schedule 4 terms used, schedule 2 as a choice, schedule 1 glossed. Out: ss 1, 2, 4, 8 (asked), 9, 16(5), (6), 23(3)-(5), 27-29, 31, 33, 35, 51-56 (the court's discretion), chapter 5 (ss 57-63), s 64, s 67(2), ss 68, 70, 71, chapters 7 and 8 (ss 75, 76 turn on a commencement date the deposited text does not state); each item and why in NOTES.md, Scope.
seat: the discloser: a person (usually a public officer, sometimes a GOC employee or any member of the public) who has information about wrongdoing in the Queensland public sector, has made or is thinking of making a public interest disclosure, and may have suffered a reprisal and want damages or another remedy
